requirements.note: All sections are present in an inset-grouped list with a large title. Account has name and email text fields and a red Sign Out with a native confirmation anchored to the button; confirming wasn't tried. Reading has a slider with small/large A glyphs, a Font row that pushes a list of five fonts, a 3-segment spacing control and a live preview. Appearance offers System/Light/Dark/Sepia with swatches and a checkmark. Library has Sort By (5 options) and two switches. Notifications: turning the master switch on reveals a Daily Reminder time picker and three switches, and asks iOS for notification permission. Storage shows a Books/Cache usage bar and sizes; Clear Cache confirms, then shows None and disables itself. About shows the version, Privacy and Terms push readable text screens, and Rate the App shows the system review prompt.
Font and Sort By push checkmark lists the way iOS Settings does. The reminder time uses the native compact time picker with a wheel popover.
The preview updates at once for font (Palatino), size (27 pt) and spacing (Relaxed). The Font row's value is drawn in the chosen font.
After relaunch the name edit, size, font, spacing, Sepia theme, sort order, notifications on, 10:00 PM reminder, Recommendations on and cleared cache were all kept.

Reset All Settings at the bottom confirms first, then restores reading, appearance, library and notification defaults and keeps the account; the reset also held after relaunch. The footer says when everything is already at its defaults.

bugs: With the Sepia theme, the pushed Font and Sort By screens stay plain light grey/white while the main list is tinted sepia, so the theme is applied unevenly.
tells: The Daily Reminder row is 66 pt tall while the switch rows beside it are 52 pt.
Selected rows and the slider use a brown accent under Sepia but blue otherwise. This is defensible, but the accent changes between screens.
At the largest text size the Name and Email fields truncate ("Jane XApple…") instead of wrapping. Line breaks are hyphenated and excused.
A.scroll: This is a native collection view: slow drags track the finger, flings decelerate and rubber-band, tapping the status bar scrolls to the top, and the nav bar collapses into a blurred inline title. I saw no blank rows, pop-in or stutter.

requirements.note: All sections are present in an inset-grouped list with a large title and helpful section footers. Sign Out confirms with a native alert; confirming swaps the section to 'Not signed in' with a Sign In row, which restores the account. Reading has a slider, a separate Font Size value row, a Font row pushing five fonts, a 3-segment spacing control and a preview card with a summary caption. Appearance offers System/Light/Dark/Sepia as checkmark rows. Library has Sort By (4 options) and two switches. Notifications: the master switch shows and hides a time picker and three switches. Storage lists Used, Downloaded and Cache; Clear Cache uses an alert and the cache then reads 'Zero KB' with the button disabled. About has the version, Privacy and Terms text screens and Rate the App.
Font and Sort By push checkmark lists with a footer, like iOS Settings. The reminder uses the native compact time picker.
The preview updates live for font, size (28 pt) and spacing. Under Sepia the preview card turns warm paper with brown text.
After relaunch the name, size, font, spacing, Dark theme, sort order, notification toggles, 10:00 PM reminder and cleared cache were all kept.
Reset All Settings confirms with an alert (Cancel/Reset), restores every default and keeps the account; the reset held after relaunch.

bugs: Rate the App leaves the app and opens Safari, which says "address is invalid", instead of showing an in-app review prompt. This may only happen in the simulator.
Turning Allow Notifications on never asks iOS for notification permission.
The Privacy Policy and Terms rows carry hidden stale text that VoiceOver would read ("Georgia" and "18 pt", copied from the font rows).
tells: The Font Size slider sits in its own row above a separate 'Font Size 18 pt' row, so the slider has no label beside it. This is a slightly unusual layout.
Sepia only tints the preview card; the rest of the app stays light. A footer says so, but a Sepia theme that doesn't theme the app feels thin.
An empty cache reads 'Zero KB', which is raw formatter output.
At the largest text size the Email field truncates ("jordan.lee@e…"). Line breaks are hyphenated and excused.
B.scroll: This is a native collection view with the same feel: smooth tracking, proper deceleration and rubber-banding, a collapsing large title, and no blank or popping rows.

why: Both are convincing native inset-grouped settings screens that pass every requirement, persist everything and reset correctly. A goes further in ways a user feels: it asks for real notification permission, shows the system rating prompt instead of a broken Safari hand-off, has a storage usage bar, and lets Sepia actually tint the app. B is slightly better on sign-out handling and theme consistency on pushed screens, but has more small rough edges.
